title: Financial Terms
author: 637a4e2c89ac12120fbab5de
chapter_outcomes: Advantages and disadvantages of different sources of start-up funding, funding for continuing trade and expansion

Sources for start up funding including: personal savings (used as owners' capital), family and friends, bank overdrafts, loans, leasing and mortgages, community sources, including charities and social enterprises, grants and subsidies, crowdfunding, selling shares
Sources for funding for continuing trade and expansion including: personal savings (used as owners' capital), retained profit, private institutions, venture capital, issuing shares
Advantages and disadvantages of trade credit for entrepreneurs and suppliers (trade payables), entrepreneurs and customers (trade receivables)

Explain financial terms and tools, including cash flow forecasts (cash inflows, cash outflows, surplus, deficit), break-even analysis (variable costs, fixed costs, total cost, contribution), and income statements (profit and loss, income, revenue, expenditure, debt), and define and provide examples of terms and make calculations where appropriate
The purpose and importance of keeping accurate financial records and understand the purpose of income statements and budgets, including cash flow forecasts
Reasons for keeping accurate financial records include: the need to provide a true and fair view to stakeholders, legal and taxation purposes, forecasting, decision-making for owners/shareholders
How to prepare a simple budget, including a cash flow forecast, and an income statement for an enterprise with the ablility to make simple calculations in relation to pre-released case study.
